items.q: on Broadway, it was Count Basie, Frank Sinatra, and Ella Fitzgerald. And then we went out on a little tour in a couple of cities, same group.

ctx.x: What about like playing behind Sinatra or Benny Goodman? Would those stand out as times like that?

Well I didn’t play per se behind Frank. We did work with Frank Sinatra on a number of occasions. Frank had his own drummer, Irv Cottler, the great Irv Cottler, and I was able to hang out with Irv a little bit, and actually met Sinatra. We had a little chat one night

backstage which was just delightful. So I was in the area. I could see what was happening. And that was great. It was scary enough being around their — on Broadway, it was Count Basie, Frank Sinatra, and Ella Fitzgerald. And then we went out on a little tour in a couple of cities, same group. Then we went over to the Palladium and we did a couple of weeks at the Palladium in London with Frank Sinatra, Sarah Vaughan and Count Basie. items.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Butch has supported such stellar artists as Tony Bennett, Joe Williams, Lena Horne, Dave Brubeck and Frank Sinatra.

ctx.x: Charles “Butch” Miles is a well known figure on the national and international jazz scene. Born on July 4, 1944, he grew up in Charlestown, West Virginia. He took to the drums early on and became one of the youngest drummers to ever drive the Count Basie band. Butch has supported such stellar artists as Tony Bennett, Joe Williams, Lena Horne, Dave Brubeck and Frank Sinatra. His travels have taken him from South America to the Far East and his motion picture credits include “The Last of the Blue Devils” with Count…
Butch was interviewed at the Paradise Valley Jazz Party in Scottsdale, Arizona on March 4, 1995 by Dr. Michael Woods and Monk Rowe.
